title: Key rotation stability & queue probe notes
content:
Quick notes and scratchpad for the intermittent 401/429 bursts we've been seeing when clients rotate API keys. Collecting commands, raw snippets, hypotheses, and short experiments to reproduce.

Summary:
- Symptom: short (1-3 minute) bursts of 401s followed by 429s for cohorts of clients around key rotation windows. Some clients see 401 immediately, others get 429s for up to ~2 minutes after.
- Likely interaction: key rotation + quota bookkeeping + gateway cache = temporary mismatch between auth/token cache and quota counters.
- Goal: produce minimal repro and mitigation (soft backoff jitter on rotation + pre-warm counters).

Observed timeline (single incident sample):
- 2026-02-14T16:02:10Z: client cohort A starts rotating keys (roll every 60s, stagger 0s).
- 2026-02-14T16:02:12Z: spike of 401 responses at edge (approx 1200 req/min for cohort).
- 2026-02-14T16:03:05Z: 401s drop, 429s increase for same client IPs (quota enforcement kicks in).
- 2026-02-14T16:04:40Z: traffic returns to normal after ~2.5 minutes.

Commands / queries used during triage:
- Pull auth logs for 16:00-16:10 window (GCP logging example):
  gcloud logging read "resource.type=\"http_load_balancer\" AND timestamp>\"2026-02-14T16:00:00Z\" AND timestamp<\"2026-02-14T16:10:00Z\"" --project redwood-prod --format json > /tmp/auth-window.json

- Quick grep for 401/429 counts:
  jq -r '.[]|.jsonPayload.httpStatus' /tmp/auth-window.json | sort | uniq -c

- Fetch raw headers for a failing request from edge logs: (example extracted)
  date: 2026-02-14T16:02:12.243Z
  host: api.redwood.ai
  x-forwarded-for: 34.82.XXX.XXX
  authorization: Bearer [redacted-key-id=rot-1234;sig=xxxx]
  x-auth-cache-hit: false

- cURL repro (client sim):
  for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROTATING" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete & done

- Local repro script notes: rotate key every 30s, N parallel clients, no retry jitter -> reliably produces 401->429 pattern when N>50 and rotation start is synced.

Representative log fragments (sanitized):
  [edge] 2026-02-14T16:02:12Z client=acct-42 key=rot-1234 -> 401 Unauthorized (auth-service: unknown-key)
  [auth] 2026-02-14T16:02:12Z key-lookup rot-1234: cache-miss -> backend-lookup -> valid
  [edge] 2026-02-14T16:02:13Z key=rot-1234 -> 429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: 60r/min)
  [quota] 2026-02-14T16:02:13Z quota-inc acct-42 window=2026-02-14T16:02:00-16:03:00 count=62 limit=60\n

Notes on what I saw in traces:
- Trace shows two fast paths: auth cache layer (memcached) and backend authoritative key db (spanner). When cache-miss + simultaneous backend lookup, some requests see late writes of key metadata leading to a transient "unknown-key" (401) while others proceed and later hit quota (429).
- There is a race when key metadata (quota bucket id, tier) is updated during rotation: some requests use old bucket counters, some new. If rotation increments or resets counters, overlapping windows can make a client appear to exceed quota.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Synchronized rotation causes sudden fan-out of backend key validations. Cache misses spike; some requests get 401 if backend lookup hasn't fully replicated key metadata to the layer that the edge expects.
2) Quota bucket assignment changes on rotation (new key maps to a fresh bucket with separate window) and the per-key limiter doesn't gracefully merge residual in-flight tokens -> 429s.
3) Gateway or CDN caches auth decisions for very short TTLs; during rotation the cache TTLs expire and result in bursts to the auth backend.
4) Clients that aggressively retry with no jitter amplify the immediate quota exceed once some start succeeding.

Short experiments tried so far:
- Staggered rotations: ran client cohorts with 5s random jitter on rotation -> failure rate dropped ~80% in local test.
- Increased memcached size and TTL from 2s -> 10s for key metadata -> reduced backend lookup QPS but still observed 401->429 in very large churn test.
- Pre-warm sequence: when issuing new key, ping an internal endpoint to initialize quota counters -> reduced 429 tail in test.
- Added 200ms random retry jitter on client retries -> noticeably smoother tail.

Mitigations to test / propose:
- Server-side: when issuing new key, perform server-side pre-warm of quota bucket and prime auth cache across edge nodes (async replication + ack). Mark key state as "preready" only after priming.
- Server-side fallback: if auth-backend returns unknown-key but backend lookup is in-flight, return 202 or a soft-accept with low-rate token rather than 401 to allow polite retries. (Risk: security semantics?)
- Client-side guidance: recommend randomized rotation jitter and exponential backoff with cap for retries. Add snippet to SDK quickstart.
- Rate-limiter change: on key rotation, treat new key as having a grace allowance equal to X% of previous key's unused capacity for first window.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Repro scale: what real-world cohort size corresponds to our incidents? (logs show ~200 active clients per second hitting rotate window in one customer). Need to correlate with billing/usage metrics.
- Replication lag: measure p99 propagation time for new key metadata across auth-cache replicas.
- Security: evaluate the soft-accept idea with security team. Are there CSP implications?
- Product: communicate mitigation recommendations to customers that do high-frequency rotation. Add to docs.

Next steps (short):
- Run a controlled experiment with 3 client cohorts: immediate rotation, 5s jitter, random 0-30s jitter. Capture 401/429 distribution and auth-backend QPS. (Owner: Jordan)
- Add a small pre-warm path to the key issuance flow in staging and test with warm-up on quota backend. (Owner: Priya)
- Instrument cache TTLs and replication time (Owner: Marco)

Notes to self: keep this as a living doc rather than Confluence until we have a repro artifact and concrete numbers. Save raw traces to /tmp/rotation-traces-20260214.tgz and link in Confluence once attached.

Snippets to copy into ticket:
- "Observed 401 spikes at key rotation followed by transient 429s for same client cohort; timeline suggests race between auth cache and quota assignment. Repro with synchronized rotations >50 clients."

-- end of scratchpad --
